desc:
Ecom Swift LLC improves Android app onboarding and paywall optimization so that more installs become regular users. We rework the first-run path, the upgrade screen and key prompts, and add tracking to show where people leave.

## What is Android app onboarding and paywall optimization?

It is the work of improving the path a new user takes from first launch to first useful result, and the screen where they decide to pay. Onboarding explains the value quickly and asks for only what is needed. The paywall, or upgrade screen, explains what a paid plan adds and makes the choice clear.

Both sit at the moments where most users decide to stay or leave. Small changes in wording, order and layout there can change behavior without touching the rest of the app.

## Why installs alone do not build a business

An install is only a promise. Many people open an app once, meet a long sign-up form, a permission request they do not understand or a screen full of options, and never return. Paid ads and store traffic are wasted when the first minute loses people.

Without tracking, the owner sees downloads going up and revenue staying flat, and cannot tell why. The fix starts with seeing where users stop.

## How the changes affect retention and upgrades

Onboarding works when it shortens the distance to the first win. If a note-taking app lets you write a note on the first screen, the value is felt at once. If it asks for an account, a profile photo and three permissions first, patience runs out.

A paywall works when the user understands the benefit before the price. Clear plan names, honest trial wording, a visible close button and a restore option build trust. Prompts for notifications and ratings work best after a good moment, such as a finished task, not at launch. We cannot promise a specific increase, because results depend on your product, audience and traffic. We can promise a clearer path and the data to judge it.

## What a conversion project includes

- A walkthrough of your current first-run path, from first launch to first win.
- A short list of friction points, ranked by likely impact.
- Onboarding screens rebuilt with plain, benefit-led wording.
- An upgrade screen that shows plans, trial terms and restore purchases clearly.
- A notification permission flow that explains the reason before the system dialog appears.
- Button and message text rewritten to be specific.
- Event tracking on the actions that matter, such as sign-up, first win and purchase start.
- In-app rating prompts placed after positive moments and within Google Play policy.
- Screen variants and Firebase Remote Config setup for comparing versions, in the larger package.
- A short reading guide so you can interpret the results.

## How we work

We trace the journey as a new user, then agree which screens to change. The Basic package covers the path walkthrough, one rebuilt screen, rewritten text and tracking on three key actions. Standard rebuilds the onboarding flow and upgrade screen, expands tracking and improves the notification request. Premium adds screen variants, a test setup and a plan for reading the outcomes.

Every change is built in your own project and tested before we hand over a build. You receive a before and after summary.

## Good habits and pitfalls for onboarding and upgrade screens

**Do:**
- Name the single action that best predicts a returning user.
- Show the value of the app before asking for an account.
- Explain every permission in the user's terms.
- Let people see what they are buying before they pay.
- Compare versions one change at a time.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding the close button or the cancel path on the upgrade screen.
- Asking for a rating at launch.
- Pushing several notification requests in a row.
- Using wording that implies a fake countdown or false scarcity.
- Judging a test on a handful of users.

## Who this is for

This service suits an app owner who pays for installs but sees users vanish after the first session. It suits a subscription app whose upgrade screen has never been tested. It also suits a developer who built the product well but has no analytics and no clear view of user behavior.

## What we need from you

Send the app link or build, a test account and any analytics you already have. A note on your plans and pricing helps. We work in your own project and accounts, and we never need your passwords. Repository access is given as a collaborator, and Play Console access as a limited user.
